mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines over 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.0% for two months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous month-over-month increases in housing starts and retail sales indicate robust consumer demand that drives corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increase month-over-month, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes with industrial production growth above 1.5%, supply chain pressures ease and profit margins expand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances during late-cycle expansion with INDPRO growth >1.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Quarterly real GDP growth exceeding 2.0% signals strong economic momentum that supports corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances where GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% quarter-over-quarter, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% triggers monetary tightening expectations that increase discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL y/y growth exceeds 3.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In tight labor market regimes with unemployment rate below 4.0%, strong job growth supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances during tight labor market regimes (UNRATE < 4.0%), or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in federal funds rate and unemployment rate signal accommodative monetary policy combined with labor market strength, boosting consumer confidence and corporate investment to produce positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing and labor market strengthening
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE decline month-over-month, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.
